observations: docs/traps.md, 'Clones can be shallow', ends 'CI checks out full history.' That holds for verdict.yml, release.yml and clean-room.yml (fetch-depth: 0) but not for ci.yml, whose actions/checkout is depth 1, where npm test and every verifier suite run; verify/fix-budget-rule/backfill-true.test.mjs says so itself ('CI fetches one commit'). A reader who trusts the line writes a history-reading test that passes locally after --unshallow and fails or skips on ci. Worth a one-line fix: 'ci.yml checks out one commit; verdict.yml full history.'

docs/traps.md, 'The container signs commits', says signed temp-repo commits 'get different shas on every run'. Here the SSH signature is deterministic: with fixed dates two signed runs gave the same sha. The trap stands because no machine without this key can make that sha, which is what the doc's next clause says.
